document.title: TFXX01: Afghanistan: Reaction to U.S. Strikes Follows Predicable Lines: Taliban Angry, Their Opponents Support U.S.
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] After the air strikes, Mullah Omar declares the Taliban will never hand over bin Laden. Hamid Karzai tells the Department that bin Laden is on the move and that several Taliban officials are unhappy with Omar for bringing the U.S. against Afghanistan. Overall the strikes have not produced an anti-American reaction in Afghanistan; many Afghans see bin Laden as more of a burden than a blessing.

events.description: US strikes on Bin Ladin's terrorist camps in Khost Province.
Mullah Omar, via AIP, denounces US attack and vows not to hand over Bin Ladin.
Dostam phones NIMA representative Zeki from Bamiyan expressing support for the US.
Several thousand Afghan refugees demonstrate in Peshawar area; possibly violent.
Mullah Malang meets Embassy poloff and speculates on Bin Ladin's Kandahar locations.
Several thousand Afghan refugees in NWFP camps demonstrated in the Peshawar area against the U.S. strikes; unconfirmed reports of violence.
Hamid Karzai and Abdul Ahad Karzai expressed strong support for U.S. strikes on Afghanistan.
Mohammad Hakim Ayubi's group issued a statement expressing sorrow over the U.S. action while noting concern about Afghanistan as a base for terrorism.
Hamid Gailani said 99 percent of Afghans he met were angered the Taliban failed to drive bin Ladin out.
Embassy Islamabad sent cable assessing reaction to U.S. strikes.
U.S. strikes on bin Ladin's terrorist camps in Khost province.
Mullah Omar, via AIP, denounced the U.S. attack and vowed never to hand over bin Ladin.
Mutmain criticized the strikes and gave casualty figures of 30 dead, 40 wounded.
Hamid Karzai told POLOFF bin Ladin was reportedly on the move.
Mullah Malang met POLOFF and speculated bin Ladin was in Kandahar area.
Dostam telephoned Zeki from Bamiyan expressing support for the U.S. strikes.
Raza Naz spoke to POLOFF about Wahdat's reaction to strikes.

sources_cited: Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) interview with Mullah Omar
key_claims: Mullah Omar vowed the Taliban would never hand over Bin Ladin and would keep providing safe haven after the 20 Aug 1998 strikes.
Bin Ladin was believed to have been flushed out of Khost and to be in the Kandahar area, possibly at the airport barracks, the house built for Omar, or a complex near Dahla.
The anti-Taliban Northern Alliance factions (NIMA, Wahdat, Jamiat) strongly supported the US strikes.
Independent Pashtuns such as Karzai and Gailani were favorable and said many Taliban officials were displeased with Omar.
Embassy assessed there was little nationalistic backlash, though refugees demonstrated in Peshawar.
Bin Ladin was financially supporting the Taliban, making him opposed by the Northern Alliance.
